claim_summary: For an exact radial power-law parent distribution with source-count exponent q>0 and independent fixed-arithmetic-mean lognormal luminosity, increasing log-variance strictly lowers a finite flux-limited detection fraction when q<=2 or mean luminosity meets the survey-edge threshold; when q>2 and mean luminosity is below the edge threshold there is a unique optimal positive log-variance with an explicit integral equation and sharp faint-mean asymptotic.
scientific_integrity: A self-contained analytic proof is supplied; a finite standard-library checker provides independent numerical consistency diagnostics but cannot establish uniqueness over infinite parameter ranges. General count-selection formulae and inverse-square visibility are known prior work and are not claimed as novel. No independent scientific review has been performed.
scientific_limitations: Finite parent survey volume, exact power-law radial CDF, independence of intrinsic luminosity and distance, sharp inverse-square flux cutoff, and fixed arithmetic mean are essential. The result is conditional catalog-inclusion probability, not observed astrophysical luminosity evolution or a strategy for changing real dispersion. Historical priority beyond examined records remains provisional; mathematical-finance literature on lognormal capped-power payoffs is a possible antecedent.
title: A sharp source-count exponent transition for luminosity scatter in finite flux-limited surveys
